items.statement: For every prime p ∉ E_bgs: (a) Aut⁺(Π) acts transitively on X*(p) and on M*(p); (b) M(SL₂(F_p))‾^{abs}_{−2} := M(SL₂(F_p))‾_{−2}/D(p) is connected; (c) both X and M satisfy strong approximation mod p.
items.note: Part (c) uses that reduction X(ℤ) → X(F_p) is Aut(Π)-equivariant and that the orbits of (0,0,0) and (3,3,3) exhaust X(F_p)/Aut(Π); strong approximation at 3 is checked by hand. If the remaining finite computation confirms the conjecture, Proposition 5.3.3 shows there are no congruence conditions on Markoff numbers beyond Frobenius's.

items.name: Strong approximation modulo squarefree integers (Theorem 5.5.8)
items.statement: Let p₁,…,p_r ∉ E_bgs be distinct primes each satisfying the Meiri–Puder condition MP(p): p ≡ 1 mod 4, or the order of (3+√5)/2 in F_{p²} is at least (3/2)√(p+1). Put n := p₁⋯p_r and let X*(n) ⊂ X(ℤ/nℤ) be the solutions not reducing to (0,0,0) modulo any p_i. Then (a) Aut(Π) acts transitively on X*(n); (b) X and M satisfy strong approximation mod n.
items.note: MP(p) holds for a density-one set of primes, and for all p ≡ 1 mod 4. Meiri–Puder is an input the atlas does not cover and is listed under prerequisites.

items.name: Congruences for generalized Markoff equations in terms of ω (Theorem 5.5.9)
items.statement: Suppose ω ∈ F_{q²}^× satisfies t := ω + ω^{−1} ∈ F_q − {2,−2}, let ℓ be an odd prime with ord_ℓ(|ω|) = r and ord_ℓ(q(q−1)) = r+s, and let P be an F_q-point of x²+y²+z²−xyz = t+2 with at least two coordinates nonzero. Then the Aut⁺(Π)-orbit of P has cardinality divisible by ℓ^{max{r−s,0}}.
items.note: This is the form of Theorem 1.2.7 stated with the auxiliary element ω; with results analogous to those of [BGS16a] for these equations it would give strong approximation for them too.

items.name: Ramification of M_p over the j-line (Propositions 5.6.1, 5.6.2)
items.statement: Let p ≥ 5 be prime and f : M_p → M(1) the forgetful map on coarse schemes, of degree p(p+3) for p ≡ 1 mod 4 and p(p−3) for p ≡ 3 mod 4. Then (a) f^{−1}(0) has exactly one unramified point and all others of index 3, so |f^{−1}(0)| = (deg f − 3)/3; (b) f^{−1}(1728) has exactly two unramified points if p ≡ 1, 7 mod 8 and none otherwise, all others of index 2, giving the four explicit formulas (p²+3p+2)/2, (p²−3p)/2, (p²+3p)/2, (p²−3p+2)/2 according to p mod 8; and (c) the number of cusps |f^{−1}(∞)| is the rot₁-orbit count of Proposition 5.3.5.
items.locator: arXiv:2011.12940v2 (19 June 2021), §5.6, pp. 84–85, Propositions 5.6.1 and 5.6.2, with the ramification at j = 0, 1728 from [BBCL20, Proposition 3.3.2]
items.note: The ramification indices 3 and 2 come from the fixed points of γ₀ and γ₁₇₂₈ acting on X*(p). Tests: the degree formula at p = 5 is 40.

items.name: The genus formula and finiteness (Theorems 5.6.3, 5.6.4)
items.statement: For p ≥ 5 prime, the smooth compactification of M(SL₂(F_p))‾_{−2} is a disjoint union of two copies of M_p‾, and for p ∉ E_bgs, M_p‾ is a smooth curve of genus p²/12 − ((p−1)/4)Φ(p−1) − ((p+1)/4)Φ(p+1) + ε(p), with ε(p) = (7/8)p − 29/24, (5/8)p + 19/24, (7/8)p − 17/24, (5/8)p + 7/24 according as p ≡ 1, 3, 5, 7 mod 8; in particular genus(M_p‾) ≥ p²/12 − (1/2)(p−1)^{3/2} − (1/2)(p+1)^{3/2} + p/2 for all p ≥ 5. For p ≥ 13 with p ∉ E_bgs the genus is ≥ 2, while for p = 5, 7, 11 it is 0, 0, 1; hence for p ≥ 13, p ∉ E_bgs and any number field K only finitely many elliptic curves admit an SL₂(F_p)-structure with ramification index 2p.
items.note: The genus is computed by Riemann–Hurwitz from the degree and the three ramified fibres. The finiteness consequence is Faltings' theorem applied to a curve of genus ≥ 2 over a number field.

items.name: Congruence and noncongruence modular stacks (Definition 5.6.5)
items.statement: For a subfield k ⊂ ℂ, a finite étale map f : M → M(1)_k is a congruence modular stack, and M → M(1)_k a congruence modular curve, if M_ℂ is connected and the finite-index subgroup Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) attached to f_ℂ contains the kernel of SL₂(ℤ) → SL₂(ℤ/n) for some n; otherwise it is noncongruence.
items.note: Chen conjectures in [Che18] that the components of M(G) are noncongruence for all nonsolvable G; the problem is central to the geometric approach to the unbounded denominators conjecture for noncongruence modular forms.

items.name: Noncongruence for a density-one set of primes (Theorem 5.6.6, Corollary 5.6.8)
items.statement: Let P_MP be the set of primes p ≥ 5 with p ∉ E_bgs satisfying MP(p), a set of density one. For p ∈ P_MP the stack M(PSL₂(F_p))^{abs}_{−2} is connected of degree d_p = p(p+3)/4 or p(p−3)/4 over M(1) according as p ≡ 1 or 3 mod 4, and its monodromy group over M(1) is the full symmetric group S_{d_p} for p ≡ 5, 7, 9, 11 mod 16 and the alternating group A_{d_p} for p ≡ 1, 3, 13, 15 mod 16. Consequently, for p ∈ P_MP the stacks M(PSL₂(F_p))^{abs}_{−2} and M(SL₂(F_p))^{abs}_{−2} are noncongruence.
items.locator: arXiv:2011.12940v2 (19 June 2021), §5.6, pp. 86–87, Theorem 5.6.6 and Corollary 5.6.8, using [MP+18] and [BBCL20, §3.3]
items.note: A congruence cover would have solvable-by-PSL₂ monodromy, not a full alternating or symmetric group of large degree. Conjecturally the theorem holds for all p ≥ 5.

items.name: Noetherian approximation for prestable curves with a group action (Remark 6.1.1)
items.statement: A prestable curve C → S with an effective Cartier divisor R finite étale over a quasi-compact quasi-separated S and an S-linear action of a finite group G preserving R is the base change of the same data over some finite-type ℤ-scheme S_i, writing S as a cofiltered limit of such with affine transitions.
items.note: Used to reduce statements about prestable curves to the Noetherian case. Tests: the limit presentation of a quasi-compact quasi-separated base.

items.name: Eigenspace decomposition and henselization of invariants (Lemmas 6.1.2, 6.1.3)
items.statement: Let A be a ring with Spec A connected, e invertible in A and μ_{e,A} totally split, let M be an A-module with an A-linear action of a cyclic group ⟨g⟩ of order e, and let p_ζ(m) := (1/e)Σ_j ζ^{−j}g^j(m). Then p_ζ(M) = M_ζ := {m : gm = ζm} and ⊕_ζ p_ζ : M → ⊕_{ζ ∈ μ_e(A)} M_ζ is an isomorphism, and M ↦ M_ζ is exact. Moreover, for a ring R with an action of a finite group G, a maximal ideal m_R and m_{R^G} := m_R ∩ R^G: m_{R^G} is maximal; the henselizations R^h and (R^G)^h are local; R ⊗_{R^G} (R^G)^h ≅ R^h; and (R^G)^h ≅ (R^h)^G.
items.note: Lemma 6.1.3 needs no tameness hypothesis. These are the local tools behind the normalized coordinates of Proposition 6.1.4.

items.name: Normalized coordinates for tame balanced actions (Proposition 6.1.4)
items.statement: Let G be a finite group of order invertible on S acting S-linearly and fibrewise faithfully on a prestable curve C/S, let p be a geometric point with image s and cyclic stabiliser G_p of order e with generator g, A := O_{S,s} and R the strict local ring of C_A at p. (a) If p is smooth in its fibre, there is φ : A[z] → R identifying R with the strict local ring of A[z] at (m_A,z) and G_p-equivariant for gz = ζ_e z. (b) If p is a node whose G_p-action preserves the two branches of the cotangent space and lands in SL of it, there are a ∈ m_A and φ : A[z,w]/(zw−a) → R identifying R with the strict local ring at (m_A,z,w) and G_p-equivariant for gz = ζ_e z, gw = ζ_e^{−1}w. In particular the quotient C → C/G satisfies conditions (4), (5) and (6) of Definition 2.1.4.
items.note: This is the precise sense in which a balanced action gives the admissible local models, and it justifies Remark 2.1.5(d).

items.name: The normalizer of SL_n(F_q) in GL_n(F_q‾) (Proposition 6.2.1)
items.statement: For a prime power q and n ≥ 1, N_{GL_n(F_q‾)}(SL_n(F_q)) = F_q‾^× · GL_n(F_q), and the same holds with GL_n(F_q) in place of SL_n(F_q).
items.note: Used to show that two absolutely irreducible representations conjugate over F_q‾ are conjugate over F_q, in the second proof of Theorem 5.2.10.

items.name: Images of absolutely irreducible representations into SL₂(F_q) (Proposition 6.3.1)
items.statement: Let ϕ : Π → SL₂(F_q) be absolutely irreducible with image G and image G‾ in PSL₂(F_q). Then G‾ is dihedral D_{2n} (n ≥ 2), A₄, A₅, S₅, PGL₂(F_q‾)-conjugate to PSL₂(F_{q′}) for some q′ | q, or PGL₂(F_q‾)-conjugate to PGL₂(F_{q′}) with q′² | q; in each case G is a central extension of G‾ by Z := Z(SL₂(F_q)), and outside the dihedral case the normalizer and centralizer of G in GL₂(F_q) satisfy |N/C| ≤ 2.
items.locator: arXiv:2011.12940v2 (19 June 2021), §6.3, pp. 89–90, Proposition 6.3.1, following Macbeath [Mac69, §4]
items.note: This is Dickson's classification of subgroups of SL₂ in the form needed; it is absent from both libraries. It is what excludes the dihedral case in Theorem 5.3.2 and bounds d_X for proper subgroups.

items.name: Étale local rings of Deligne–Mumford stacks and deformation rings (§6.4)
items.statement: For a Deligne–Mumford stack M with representable diagonal and a point x : Spec Ω → M, the category of étale neighbourhoods is cofiltered and the étale local ring is O_{M,x} := colim Γ(U,O_U); for a scheme this is the strict henselization. Proposition 6.4.2 identifies its residue field and basic properties, Definition 6.4.3 gives the deformation functor of x₀, Proposition 6.4.5 compares the completion of the étale local ring with the universal deformation ring, and Proposition 6.4.6 gives the criterion for a map of locally Noetherian Deligne–Mumford stacks with representable diagonal to be étale in terms of the induced map of deformation functors.
items.note: R09.6 plans the comparison of the deformation functor at a geometric point with the completed local ring of the constructed scheme or stack, including stabilisers and versality; neither library has stacks, so nothing of this exists yet. Chen uses it to deduce étaleness of Adm⁰(G) → M(1) from Proposition 2.5.3.

items.name: Galois categories, fibre functors and the fundamental group
items.statement: A Galois category with a fibre functor F has Aut(F) a profinite group, the category is equivalent to the category of finite continuous Aut(F)-sets, every object decomposes into connected components, and a profinite group acting on F with the corresponding properties is the fundamental group.
items.locator: arXiv:2011.12940v2 (19 June 2021), §2.5.3, §4.6 and throughout §4, where the Galois correspondence for finite étale covers is used
items.note: Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Galois/{Basic,GaloisObjects,Prorepresentability,IsFundamentalgroup,Decomposition}.lean at the pinned commit; the audit of InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups IG.0 records the abstract theory as present and sorry-free. What is missing is the Galois category of finite étale covers of a scheme and its geometric fibre functor, which is what Chen applies it to.

items.name: Free groups and the free group of rank two
items.statement: Π is the free group of rank 2, realised as the fundamental group of a once-punctured genus-1 surface, with a positively oriented basis a, b; Aut(Π), Aut⁺(Π) (determinant 1 on the abelianisation), Out(Π) and Out⁺(Π) ≅ SL₂(ℤ) act on it.
items.note: Mathlib/GroupTheory/FreeGroup/Basic.lean gives free groups on a type with their universal property, and MulAut gives the automorphism group; the identification Out⁺(F₂) ≅ SL₂(ℤ), the action on Epi^ext and Nielsen equivalence are not in either library. Mathlib's NielsenSchreier is the unrelated theorem that subgroups of free groups are free.

items.name: Elliptic curves, the j-invariant and the discriminant
items.statement: An elliptic curve over a base is a smooth proper genus-1 curve with a section; its j-invariant identifies the coarse moduli of elliptic curves with the affine j-line.
items.note: Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Weierstrass.lean:389 defines j and :132 the discriminant Δ, over an arbitrary commutative ring, with the invariance under variable change in VariableChange.lean. Elliptic curves as schemes over a base, their moduli stack and generalized elliptic curves are not present.

items.name: SL₂ over a commutative ring, traces and commutators
items.statement: SL₂(R) for a commutative ring R, its centre {±I}, the trace, the commutator [A,B] = ABA^{−1}B^{−1}, and the conjugation action of GL₂(R).
items.note: Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/SpecialLinearGroup.lean:52 and Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Trace.lean; Tau Ceti adds SL₂(ℤ) congruence subgroups in TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/CongruenceSubgroups. The classification of subgroups of SL₂(F_q), the character variety and the trace identity of Lemma 5.2.4 are missing.

items.name: Permutation triples, monodromy and the combinatorial genus
items.statement: Covers branched over three points correspond to permutation triples with product one; the monodromy group, the automorphism group as the centraliser of the monodromy group, and the Euler characteristic or genus of a triple are the combinatorial shadow of the geometry.
items.locator: arXiv:2011.12940v2 (19 June 2021), §4.4 and §4.7, where covers of P¹ branched over {0,1,∞} and their component graphs are analysed
items.note: Tau Ceti has permutation triples with product one, isomorphism by simultaneous conjugation, the automorphism group as the centraliser, the combinatorial Euler characteristic (TauCeti/Combinatorics/PermutationTriple/EulerCharacteristic.lean) and the classification of covering spaces by π₁-sets with monodromy; the audit of IG.3 records the same. Missing on the geometric side: Belyi maps, covers of P¹ branched over three points as schemes, and Riemann existence.

items.name: Euler's totient and the divisor sum Φ(n)
items.statement: φ is Euler's totient and Φ(n) := Σ_{d|n} φ(d)/d, which appears in the cusp count and the genus formula.
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/Divisors.lean and Mathlib/NumberTheory/Totient.lean give φ, the divisor set and multiplicativity; Φ is the rational-valued divisor sum built from them.

items.name: Riemann existence and branch cycles
items.statement: Finite covers of a curve branched over a prescribed finite set correspond to permutation representations of the fundamental group of its complement, with branch cycles at the punctures.
items.locator: arXiv:2011.12940v2 (19 June 2021), §2.5.1, p. 27, in the proof of Theorem 2.5.2(5), and §4.6
items.note: IG.3 plans branched covers from generating tuples with product one through Riemann existence, consuming the Tau Ceti Belyi maps roadmap for three-point covers; its audit records that the topological half exists in Tau Ceti and the geometric half does not. Chen uses the Riemann existence theorem for stacks, quoted from [Noo05, Theorem 20.4].

items.name: Faltings' theorem for curves of genus at least two
items.statement: A smooth proper curve of genus ≥ 2 over a number field has only finitely many rational points.
items.locator: arXiv:2011.12940v2 (19 June 2021), §1.2.2, p. 8, and §5.6, p. 86, in the proof of Theorem 5.6.4
items.note: RP.4 plans the Parshin reduction and the Shafarevich finiteness route to Faltings' theorem, and R28.5 plans Shafarevich finiteness itself. Chen uses it only as a black box to deduce the finiteness of elliptic curves with an SL₂(F_p)-structure of ramification index 2p.

items.name: The Riemann–Hurwitz formula for a branched cover of curves
items.statement: For a finite separable map of smooth proper curves, the genus of the source is computed from the degree, the genus of the target and the ramification indices.
items.locator: arXiv:2011.12940v2 (19 June 2021), §5.6, p. 85, used to derive Theorem 5.6.3 from Propositions 5.6.1 and 5.6.2
items.note: Layer 7 of the Tau Ceti roadmap Algebraic curves plans the different and the Hurwitz genus formula; that roadmap is existing work. Tau Ceti has the combinatorial Riemann–Hurwitz for permutation triples, but the geometric formula for a branched cover of curves is what the genus computation of §5.6 uses.

items.name: Algebraic and Deligne–Mumford stacks with their atlases
items.statement: Categories fibred in groupoids, stackification, representable diagonals, smooth and étale atlases, Deligne–Mumford and tame stacks, and the local structure theorem giving an étale cover by quotients [V/G].
items.locator: arXiv:2011.12940v2 (19 June 2021), §2.1 and §3.4, used throughout for Adm(G)‾, M(G)‾ and their coarse schemes
items.note: R09.4 plans exactly this; its reviewed audit records that there are no atlases, no algebraic stacks and no quotient stacks in either library, and that the moduli stacks of generalised elliptic curves do not exist. Everything Chen does with stacks rests on this layer.
